circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street course that winds around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds FIA Grade 1 status. It serves as the permanent venue for the Australian Grand Prix and hosts various supporting racing categories including the Supercars Championship event.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, the Red Bull Ring is a 4. 326 km circuit that has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two separate eras. The venue originally operated as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987 before undergoing renovation and renaming as the A1-Ring, subsequently staging the grand prix again between 1997 and 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital measuring approximately 6 km, ranking among the longest venues in Formula One racing. Following its first appearance as the 2016 European Grand Prix, the circuit became a permanent fixture on the calendar in 2017 under the name Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, inaugurated in 2004, is a 5. 412 km facility that hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's debut in the Middle East. Beyond F1, the venue accommodates various racing series including GP2 competition, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance events, while maintaining FIA Grade 1 certification and offering multiple track configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the 4. 657 km Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya features a balanced mix of extended straights and varied corner configurations that test all-around driving capabilities. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit spans 7. 004 km and has been hosting Formula One racing since 1925, appearing on the inaugural F1 calendar in 1950. Located near the town of Spa in Wallonia, it continues as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix, with consistent annual appearances since 1985 aside from two cancelled editions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Situated on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its role in the premier motorsport series, the venue has hosted various international racing championships including sportscar competitions and open-wheel series throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit is located in Jiading and served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before returning to the calendar in 2024. Beyond its primary Formula One event, the venue has expanded its motorsport portfolio to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone Circuit has been synonymous with British motorsport since hosting the inaugural post-war Grand Prix in 1948. The track became the venue for the first-ever World Championship race in 1950 and, after sharing hosting duties with other circuits during the 1950s-1980s, became the permanent home of the British Grand Prix from 1987 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also stages the British round of the MotoGP championship.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: Located near Budapest in Mogyoród, the Hungaroring is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One venue, the track was constructed outside the city near a highway after plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were abandoned.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 that ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues and remains mainland Europe's oldest. The venue annually hosts the Italian Grand Prix, which has been a staple of the Formula One calendar since 1949 with only one interruption in 1980 for renovations, making it one of just four circuits to appear continuously since the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue with a 155,000-person capacity. The track is renowned primarily for hosting Formula One races and the Japanese Super Formula championship series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running adjacent to Las Vegas proper and featuring the famous Las Vegas Boulevard section dotted with major hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates prominent city landmarks such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas into its racing configuration.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is named in tribute to two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix across multiple eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current configuration, though it previously staged the race on a different layout until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Built by specialist designers for the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022, the track has since expanded its use to include Formula E racing from the 2025-26 season onward with a modified configuration.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco stretches for 3. 337 kilometers through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, weaving around Monaco's harbor. Though officially named after the circuit itself, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its location primarily within that particular district of the principality.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021 before the partnership concluded in 2026. The venue, situated near the North Sea, has operated under various names throughout its history and carried a sponsorship designation from mid-2025 onwards.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit sits just north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309-kilometer Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and hosts a karting facility dedicated to Ayrton Senna's memory.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street circuit positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural 2021 running. The venue also began hosting an international electric racing series event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary street-based racing venue located around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner complexities that test multiple driving skills. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility in Austin, Texas, that currently serves as the venue for the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside hosting MotoGP and endurance racing events. The track has established itself as a premier motorsport destination, having previously accommodated various racing series including IndyCar and Australian V8 Supercars competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, racing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships, both achieved with Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 race victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seater racing, Alonso has established himself as an accomplished endurance competitor, winning the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship and claiming multiple victories at prestigious events including Le Mans and Daytona, making him the sole driver to have captured both a Formula One drivers' title and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes' Formula One lineup in 2025 and has secured eight race victories during his early career in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Haas, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his racing experience to the grid.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Valtteri Bottas, a Finnish driver competing for Cadillac in Formula One, achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Alejandro Colapinto currently races for Alpine in Formula One.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver competing in European prototype racing with Nielsen Racing while serving as a backup driver for Haas in Formula One, where he has started seven races during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory, achieved during his time with AlphaTauri, stands as a significant achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One racing while competing for Red Bull Racing, though he holds dual citizenship with Algeria.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has matched Michael Schumacher's record of seven world championship titles. He holds multiple records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg represents Germany in Formula One, currently racing for Audi. Beyond single-seater competition, the driver has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably capturing the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again in 2022-2024. He currently races in the World Endurance Championship for BMW through WRT and competes part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Great Britain in Formula One, driving for McLaren, where he secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship title. The 13-time Grand Prix winner has competed at the elite level for eight seasons.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon represents France in Formula One competition, currently driving for the Haas team in his professional motorsport career.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez represents Mexico in Formula One racing with Cadillac as his current team. The experienced driver finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One spanning 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, during which he secured eight Grand Prix victories before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category driving for Proton Competition, following prior experience in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver competing in Formula One, currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, transitioned to a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls after competing as a full-time Formula One competitor from 2021 through 2025, taking on backup responsibilities starting in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, where he has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top series from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the only Chinese-born driver to have raced in Formula One.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine since 2021, representing Renault's sports car division while serving as the manufacturer's official works team. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the squad transitioned from being a factory operation to an independent entity operating under the Alpine Racing banner.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automobile maker, has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations, with its present iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, having entered every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The team, colloquially known as "the Prancing Horse" after their emblematic logo, maintains an unmatched record of continuous participation throughout the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad first competing in the 2016 championship season. Leadership recently transitioned when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal role in early 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who had held the position since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Sauber was a Swiss motorsport engineering company established in 1970 that competed in Formula One from 1993 onwards as an independent constructor. The team achieved significant success in endurance racing, including a Le Mans 24 Hours victory in 1989, before undergoing numerous transformations throughout its three-decade F1 tenure. Audi acquired the team and its operations in 2024, using Sauber's chassis expertise and sporting infrastructure as the foundation for its own F1 entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group and is wholly controlled by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, based in Brackley and operating under a German license, saw Ineos join as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff in 2022. The marque's racing efforts are historically known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's expansion into a second competitive entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that entered the sport in 2024, based in Faenza with a secondary facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes. As one of two constructors owned by Red Bull GmbH, it operates alongside the main Red Bull Racing outfit within the energy drink company's motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, competing under an Austrian licence from an England-based facility, has been a dominant force in Formula One since its 2005 establishment as part of the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. The team operated under Christian Horner's leadership for two decades before Laurent Mekies assumed the team principal role in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also operates a second Formula One team, Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's prior failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of motorsport's established constructors.
